CTGAN, explicitly listed among the Python packages used alongside SDV, was run as one of several data-augmentation methods generating synthetic minority-class samples for model training.

paper-interpretable-machine-learning-mod.summary: This conference paper proposes a six-step explainable-AI framework for predicting electric-vehicle battery failure risk, combining generative data augmentation, multiple ML classifiers (MLP selected as best), LIME/SHAP explanations, domain knowledge rules, and a knowledge graph, evaluated on a small real-world EV battery dataset. CTGAN is run as the generative component that augments the sparse real-world training data, forming the 'CTGAN-LIME-KR' pipeline central to the proposed method.

paper-physics-informed-tvae-probabilisti.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed probabilistic modelling framework for fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composite coupons, where a physics-informed tabular variational autoencoder (PI-TVAE) generates physically admissible synthetic data to augment scarce experimental datasets. The augmented data is used to train Bayesian neural network and natural gradient boosting models predicting tensile strength, ultimate strain, and failure behaviour, with SHAP used for interpretability. The authors propose an evaluation framework balancing spatial accuracy, utility, and privacy, showing their NF+VAE architecture outperforms copula-based and uniform-allocation benchmarks. SDV's Gaussian copula implementation is used as one of the comparison baselines for generating synthetic populations.

The authors generate synthetic profiles with Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and VAE, evaluate fidelity, and find that an SVM trained on real data augmented with Gaussian-Copula synthetic data best predicts DDR, later validating novel inducers experimentally. All four synthetic-data generators and the fidelity metrics (column shape, column pair trend, combined similarity) were run through the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library and its SDMetrics quality-report scores, making SDV the core generative and evaluation engine of the study.

The best result is an SVM-RBF model trained on ADASYN-augmented data, while deep generative resamplers underperformed traditional adaptive oversampling. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of the six compared resampling strategies, with the authors stating their architectural parameters 'follow the SDV library defaults', making SDV's CTGAN and TVAE comparison baselines that the winning ADASYN-based method outperforms.

paper-rethinking-anonymity-claims-synthe.summary: This paper argues that anonymity claims about synthetic tabular data should be assessed from a model-centric perspective grounded in state-of-the-art privacy attacks, rather than at the level of a single released dataset, and interprets GDPR's definitions of personal data and anonymization accordingly. It compares Differential Privacy and Similarity-based Privacy Metrics as the two mechanisms commonly paired with synthetic data generation, concluding that only DP offers robust protection. CTGAN is cited only in a list of generative-model families (GANs, diffusion models, Bayesian networks, transformers) used to produce synthetic data, with no engagement with its specific design or execution.

paper-robust-intrusion-detection-machine.summary: A systematic review and proposed framework (SE-IDS) for network intrusion detection, combining Random Forest, XGBoost, and MLP classifiers in a stacked ensemble with SMOTE-based imbalance handling and SHAP-guided feature selection, evaluated across benchmark IDS datasets. The paper's literature synthesis includes a comparison table of class-imbalance handling techniques drawn from the 46 reviewed studies. CTGAN is cited and described in that table as a GAN-based conditional tabular synthesizer prone to mode collapse on ultra-rare attack subtypes, not implemented or run by the authors themselves.

paper-gan-gan-augmentation-stablecoin-20.summary: This conference paper proposes SC-GAN, a conditional GAN that generates synthetic fraudulent stablecoin transactions to counter extreme class imbalance in fraud detection datasets. The authors evaluate SC-GAN against oversampling methods (SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN) and generative baselines on a real-world USDC/USDT transaction dataset, reporting F1, AUC-PR, MCC and constraint-satisfaction metrics. CTGAN is included as one of the baseline generators in the results table, and the Synthetic Data Vault paper (Patki et al., 2016) appears only in the reference list without further discussion in the body.

paper-synthnet-vae-gan-driven-2026.summary: This paper proposes SynthNet, a hybrid VAE-GAN synthetic data generation framework paired with a LightGBM-based multi-class intrusion detection pipeline for IoT network traffic, evaluated on a CICIDS2017-derived 7-class dataset to address severe class imbalance. paper-double-layered-fully-automated-202.summary: This paper presents a two-layer data augmentation pipeline for single-channel EEG-based insomnia detection: a Modified Conventional Signal Augmentation (MCSA) step generates synthetic raw EEG signals, and a second layer applies CTGAN to synthesize tabular data from extracted EEG features, feeding classifiers such as Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Gradient Boosting. paper-water-quality-index-synthetic-2023.summary: Addresses data scarcity in water-quality-index estimation for two rivers in Peninsular Malaysia, the Selangor and the Skudai, where the Department of Environment's monthly sampling leaves only 240 points per river over 2005-2014, a shortage the authors argue is structural in developing regions and unresolved by bootstrap aggregation or adaptive synthetic sampling. It discusses realism, privacy, and utility trade-offs, surveys privacy attacks, and situates generative techniques including Gaussian copula and GAN-based methods within the levels. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited as an example of a generative technique (Gaussian copula/GAN) used at Level 3 of the hierarchy, without being run or evaluated experimentally.

preprint-treb-bert-attempt-imputing-2024.summary: This preprint proposes TREB, a BERT-based framework fine-tuned to impute missing real-valued continuous entries in tabular data, validated on the California Housing dataset and analyzed for FLOPs and carbon footprint. In its related-work discussion of generative approaches to tabular data, the authors describe CTGAN as using a conditional generator to model row probability distributions and generate realistic synthetic data, without running it as part of their own experiments. CTGAN's conditional generator concept is only cited descriptively as prior tabular generative modeling work, not used in TREB's pipeline.
preprint-treb-bert-attempt-imputing-2024.needs: The garbled byline text ('Han drk-m-s Jiang') made the third author's real name uncertain; rendered as 'Han Jiang'.

paper-dgm-tabular-dp-overview-2023.summary: Synthesises the literature on deep generative models for tabular data under differential privacy, setting variational autoencoders, normalizing flows, GANs and diffusion models in a common probabilistic notation and then tracing how each has been fitted with privacy guarantees, with attention to where the tabular setting breaks assumptions carried over from images. CTGAN is presented as the reference set of refinements for the tabular GAN, named for mode-specific normalization and conditioning vectors and for carrying both across to the VAE in the same work; later methods are described by what they replace in it, such as an inverse-CDF transform standing in for its mode-specific normalization. Nothing is run.

paper-discgan-healthcare-2023.summary: Proposes discGAN, a distributed conditional GAN for synthetic electronic health records, in which discriminators sit with the data at each site so that patient records never leave their holder, evaluated on ICU stay records by machine-learning efficacy, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-squared tests. CTGAN is the state of the art the design is written against: the literature survey gives it its own section headed as the conditional tabular model from the Synthetic Data Vault, the paper takes its account of the discrete-and-continuous modelling problem from it, and discGAN's architecture is defined by contrast, dropping the residual block the CTGAN implementation uses. CTGAN itself is not run.

preprint-research-clinic-accelerating-tr.summary: This paper presents SyntHIR, an architecture for integrating synthetic data generators, data interoperability standards (HL7 FHIR/SMART on FHIR), and tool transportability to help translate machine-learning-based clinical decision support system (CDSS) tools from research into deployable EHR-connected tools, demonstrated via a proof-of-concept deployed in Norway's largest EHR vendor (DIPS). The current implementation uses another synthetic data generator (Synthea); Synthetic Data Vault is named only as a candidate to add in future work. SDV is cited only as a synthetic data generator the authors intend to integrate later, with no experiment run using it.

preprint-lessons-learned-defending-again.summary: This paper investigates defenses against property inference attacks (PIAs) on machine learning models, proposing a 'property unlearning' post-training technique and comparing it with simpler data-preprocessing defenses such as noise addition, k-anonymization, censoring, and synthetic data generation. In one experiment on the Census tabular dataset, the authors generate an artificial version of the training data as an alternative defense strategy. CTGAN's open-source implementation is run unmodified to produce this synthetic data, without any additional steps to hide the target property.

preprint-mitigating-greenhouse-gas-emiss.summary: This paper builds a wildfire-risk prediction dataset from meteorological, vegetation, topological and powerline-distance features and applies a conditional tabular GAN to augment the training data, comparing CTGAN-augmented classifiers (decision tree, random forest, GBM, SVM, neural network) against their non-augmented baselines on two datasets. The authors describe and implement CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator architecture themselves, following Xu et al.'s design in step-by-step detail rather than invoking a package. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional vector are the concepts the whole empirical pipeline is built around, reimplemented in-house as the data augmentation engine.
preprint-mitigating-greenhouse-gas-emiss.needs: No package import, sdv/ctgan library name, or constructor hyperparameters are mentioned; classification as a from-scratch reimplementation (port) rests on the detailed step-by-step description of the algorithm rather than a library call.

paper-rcc-gan-compound-2022.summary: Replaces the per-column mask conditional vector of prior tabular GANs with a compound conditional vector that carries several columns at once, adds a regularization term over the fitted mixture parameters, and redesigns the continuous-column transformer so multivariate distributions survive encoding, targeting tables too wide for one-hot conditioning to remain tractable. CTGAN is the design the paper works from and against: it reproduces CTGAN's conditional vector definition in full before proposing its own, follows CTGAN in mapping discrete and binary columns through a tanh transformer, builds its continuous-column encoder on the same variational Gaussian mixture idea, takes the Gumbel softmax in its residual blocks from the CTGAN authors, and reports CTGAN as one of the GAN baselines it is measured against.

preprint-sec-gan-generative-adversarial-.summary: A preprint proposing a GAN-based approach ('Sec-GAN') for just-in-time software defect prediction, likely addressing class imbalance in defect datasets. No abstract, citing sentences, or full text were available to establish how the work engages with the technique. CTGAN is cited as a reference in the paper's discussion of GAN-based methods.
preprint-sec-gan-generative-adversarial-.needs: Full text or abstract needed to confirm whether CTGAN is run experimentally (e.g., for defect data augmentation) or merely cited in related work; evidence tier is metadata_only.

preprint-synthetic-observational-health-.summary: A systematic review of published research applying Generative Adversarial Networks to Observational Health Data, cataloguing algorithms, evaluation metrics, data modalities, and reproducibility practices across the field. The authors describe CTGAN's mode-specific normalization for handling non-Gaussian multi-modal continuous columns and imbalanced discrete columns, and note that HealthGAN adapted a data transformation method from the Synthetic Data Vault to map categorical features to a numerical range. Neither CTGAN nor SDV is run by the authors themselves; both are discussed and cited as prior work encountered in the reviewed literature.

preprint-benchmarking-differentially-pri.summary: This paper presents a systematic empirical benchmark comparing differentially private synthetic tabular data generation algorithms -- GAN-based, marginal-based, and workload-based -- across multiple datasets, tasks, and privacy budgets, measuring attribute-distribution similarity, pairwise correlation, and downstream ML classification accuracy. It evaluates DP variants such as DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN alongside marginal methods like MST and PrivBayes, finding GAN-based approaches often fail to beat simple baselines. SDGym, the SDV-family benchmarking harness, is explicitly run as the platform for all experiments and its metrics inspire the paper's own evaluation groups.
preprint-benchmarking-differentially-pri.needs: Reference numbering appears inconsistent (SDGym cited both as [3] the GitHub repo and mislabeled [37], which in the bibliography is actually the CTGAN NeurIPS paper) -- a likely mis-citation rather than an error in our reading.

preprint-relational-synthesis-generative.summary: A PVLDB technical report/paper that conducts a large-scale, unified experimental study of GAN-based relational data synthesis, defining a design space (network architectures, training strategies, data transformations) and comparing solutions against traditional synthesis approaches to guide practitioners. The Synthetic Data Vault, TGAN, and CTGAN papers appear only in the reference list as prior GAN-based synthesis work; the evidence confirms no SDV-family term is discussed or engaged with anywhere in the body text.

preprint-validation-medical-research-syn.summary: This preprint reports a cross-hospital validation study assessing whether statistical results from synthetic electronic medical record data reproduce those obtained from real patient data across five clinical research topics. The authors describe an institutional system that generates fictitious-patient synthetic data to let researchers analyze data before IRB approval, finding good accuracy and stability of estimates when sample sizes are large. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper as the basis for its synthetic data generation approach, without detailing which SDV component or code was actually used.
preprint-validation-medical-research-syn.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the institutional synthetic-data system directly runs SDV software or is an independent reimplementation inspired by the cited SDV paper.

preprint-modeling-tabular-conditional-ga.summary: This preprint introduces a conditional generative adversarial network for synthesizing tabular data, addressing the challenges of multimodal continuous columns and imbalanced discrete columns that defeat existing statistical and deep-learning models. The authors benchmark their model against Bayesian network baselines on 7 simulated and 8 real datasets, and cite the original SDV framework paper (Patki et al. 2016) as prior work on synthetic data generation. The work is the origin of CTGAN's conditional vector and mode-specific normalization, later incorporated as the CTGAN synthesizer within the SDV library.
preprint-modeling-tabular-conditional-ga.needs: This appears to be the original CTGAN paper itself, a first-party SDV-family work whose true importance (6) is not available under these rules; abstract text describes 'TGAN' rather than 'CTGAN', suggesting a possible version/identifier mismatch that full text would clarify.

thesis-kunar-ctabgan-2021.summary: A Delft master's thesis that first compares four GAN-based tabular synthesizers on machine learning utility, statistical similarity and privacy, then proposes CTAB-GAN, a conditional table GAN adding a mixed-type encoder, classification and information losses and a DCGAN backbone, and finally extends it to DP-CTABGAN with differentially private training evaluated under membership and attribute inference attacks. CTAB-GAN is built on CTGAN: its mixed-type encoder is derived from CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and it adopts CTGAN's conditional vector and training-by-sampling, while CTGAN is separately one of the four benchmarked baselines, run from the sdv-dev/SDGym code base.
